question: A mother on day 3 postpartum is concerned that her milk supply seems to be decreasing. She has been supplementing with formula and is feeding her baby only 4 times in 24 hours. What is the primary physiological reason her milk supply is declining?

answers.text: Oxytocin secretion from the anterior pituitary is being suppressed by the sight of formula

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Oxytocin is released from the POSTERIOR pituitary (neurohypophysis), not the anterior pituitary. Its release is triggered by suckling via the neuroendocrine reflex.

answers.text: Reduced nipple stimulation leads to inadequate prolactin release, decreasing milk synthesis

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct. Milk production follows a supply-demand principle: prolactin (anterior pituitary) is released in response to nipple stimulation. Fewer feeds mean less suckling, less prolactin, and reduced alveolar milk synthesis. Formula supplementation breaks this cycle.

answers.text: Progesterone levels rise after day 3 postpartum and directly inhibit milk synthesis in alveolar cells

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Progesterone FALLS sharply after placental delivery — this fall is what allows lactogenesis II (milk coming in). Rising progesterone is not the mechanism here; the problem is reduced suckling frequency.

answers.text: Colostrum has been fully replaced by mature milk, which requires higher suckling effort to produce

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: The transition from colostrum to transitional milk (days 3-5) does not itself reduce supply. The declining supply here is driven by infrequent feeding reducing the prolactin stimulus.

overallFeedback.feedback: Breast milk follows a supply-demand model. Prolactin (anterior pituitary) is released in response to nipple stimulation. When feeds decrease, prolactin falls and milk synthesis declines.

Well done. Breast milk production is demand-driven: suckling stimulates prolactin release (anterior pituitary), which drives alveolar milk synthesis. Fewer feeds mean less prolactin and declining supply.
